title: quantization-tradeoffs-int8-fp8-gptq-awq-kernels
content:
Purpose:
Quick internal write-up of quantization performance vs. quality tradeoffs we observed while profiling kernels and end-to-end throughput/latency on our serving runtime. This is a working doc — notes to share current numbers, profiling artifacts, and recommended next steps for rollout.

Summary / TL;DR:
- We ran a set of comparative experiments across INT8 (both static/dynamic variants), GPTQ, AWQ, and experimental FP8 on 7B/13B/30B models using the same serving runtime codepath with kernel variants: cuBLASLt-int8, CUTLASS-int8-fused, and our custom fused-attention-int8 (int8-v2).
- FP16 baseline (no quant) provides best quality and baseline throughput. GPTQ typically gives the best compression/throughput tradeoff with modest quality loss. AWQ yields smaller quality regressions vs GPTQ in many cases but incurs slightly higher compute cost in our current kernel implementation. INT8 dynamic/static (non-GPTQ/AWQ) shows biggest quality drop unless per-channel calibration + PER-MATRIX rescaling is applied. FP8 (experimental) shows near-FP16 quality at lower memory but is dependent on hardware/CUDA stack maturity and has fewer optimized kernels available.
- Kernel choice matters: cuBLASLt-int8 provides stable throughput for GEMM-heavy layers, CUTLASS-fused achieves higher throughput on sequences < 512 and when attention is fused; our int8-v2 kernel is promising for KV-cache heavy workloads but needs more tuning.

Goals of these experiments:
- Quantify: tokens/sec, p95 latency, GPU memory footprint, and accuracy delta vs FP16 baseline (perplexity on LM eval set + MMLU subset).
- Surface kernel-level hotspots (GEMM, attention softmax, KV cache copy).
- Produce recommendations for default quantization profile in hosted vs dedicated offerings.

Hardware / software baseline:
- GPU: A100 40GB, PCIe; also spot checks on H100 80GB for FP8 experiments.
- CUDA: 12.1 for H100 FP8 runs, 11.8 for A100 experiments. cuBLAS / cuBLASLt versions matched to driver.
- Serving runtime: release candidate branch quant-bench-2025 (same allocator, same batching semantics).
- Profiling: Nsight Systems (+trace), nvtx markers in runtime, and custom lightweight in-process timers. Also used perf counters for memory bandwidth sampling.

Models & datasets:
- Models: redwood-open-7B, redwood-open-13B, community-30B (decoder-only LLaMA style weights used after conversion).
- Evaluation: 1) LM devset (5k short sequences) for perplexity; 2) MMLU subset (12 multiclass tasks) for accuracy delta; 3) latency/throughput microbench: 1k requests with seq in {64,256,1024}.

Quantization methods tested:
- FP16 baseline (reference)
- INT8-dynamic (runtime quantization with on-the-fly range estimates)
- INT8-static (calibration with representative dataset, per-channel scales)
- GPTQ (post-training quantization with per-group quantizers and Hessian-aware adjustments)
- AWQ (adaptive weight quantization - published AWQ variant; tested with our conversion toolchain)
- FP8 (E4M3-like format, experimental conversion)

Kernels tested:
- cuBLASLt-int8 (vendor GEMM path for int8 matmul)
- CUTLASS-int8-fused (open-source CUTLASS kernels with fused attention/epilogue)
- int8-v1 (legacy custom GEMM/attention fused kernel in runtime)
- int8-v2 (new fused attention + KV-friendly layout optimized for streaming)
- fp8-fallback (FP16 kernel with data converted on the fly — used for functionality checks)

Key results (representative / median numbers):
- 7B (seq=256, batch=1):
  - FP16 baseline: 1280 tokens/s, p95=24ms, PPL(dev)=9.7, MMLU delta=0.0
  - GPTQ (int4/8 hybrid): 1960 tokens/s (+53%), p95=18ms, PPL=10.6 (+0.9), MMLU -0.7%
  - AWQ (int4/8 hybrid): 1840 tokens/s (+44%), p95=19ms, PPL=10.2 (+0.5), MMLU -0.3%
  - INT8-static (per-channel cal): 1700 tokens/s (+33%), p95=20ms, PPL=11.8 (+2.1), MMLU -2.3%
  - FP8 (experimental): 1200 tokens/s (-6%), p95=26ms, PPL=9.9 (+0.2), MMLU -0.2%

- 30B (seq=1024, batch=1):
  - FP16 baseline: 260 tokens/s, p95=120ms, PPL=8.1
  - GPTQ: 420 tokens/s (+62%), p95=72ms, PPL=8.7 (+0.6)
  - AWQ: 390 tokens/s (+50%), p95=82ms, PPL=8.4 (+0.3)
  - INT8-static: 360 tokens/s (+38%), p95=90ms, PPL=9.6 (+1.5)
  - FP8: 250 tokens/s (-4%), p95=125ms, PPL=8.2 (+0.1)

Observations / kernel-level notes:
- cuBLASLt-int8 delivers consistent performance on large GEMMs but suffers on batched small-matmul patterns (e.g., split-attention) — here CUTLASS-fused or int8-v2 wins.
- int8-v2 shows better memory access patterns for KV-cache streaming: reduces memory copy overhead by ~20% vs int8-v1 and improves tail latency on streaming scenarios by ~10–15%.
- AWQ conversion produced weights that still benefitted from our per-tile GEMM kernels; however our current packing/epilogue code is not yet optimal for AWQ scale layouts, so AWQ runs are ~95% of GPTQ throughput in current build.
- FP8 results: quality is near-FP16 but there are two practical issues: lack of mature fused kernels (we fell back to FP16 kernels with conversion) which hurts throughput, and H100-only reliability with current toolchain.

Quality tradeoffs and recommendations:
- Default for hosted API (latency-sensitive, cost-conscious): GPTQ for >13B models (best tokens/sec vs quality). For 7B models AWQ is attractive if we prioritize slightly better accuracy at small throughput cost.
- Dedicated (predictable capacity): offer both GPTQ and FP16 options; allow customers to pin FP16 if they need exact baseline quality.
- Private/on-prem: provide a compatibility matrix — recommend FP16 if H100/FP8 stack is not validated in customer env; otherwise offer AWQ as quality-first quant option.

Operational notes / safety checks:
- Quantized models require extensive eval on customer prompt sets — observed corner cases where GPTQ produced hallucinations in <0.1% prompts.
- KV-cache numerical stability: some INT8 static conversions without proper rescale cause token corruption at long sequences >2048. Need additional tests for rolling-off scales and cache flush behavior.

Next actions / TODOs:
- Re-run key experiments with batched requests (batch=4/8) to measure batching behavior for int8-v2 and CUTLASS-fused.
- Implement AWQ-optimized epilogue/packing in runtime (low priority perf task assigned to Luis).
- Add automated eval harness for customer-specific prompt sets (integrate with Optimize/console eval infra).
- Longer-run stability tests for FP8 on H100 fleet and driver edge-cases (esp. CUDA 12.2).
- Add telemetry flags to surface quantization-mode per request in logs for debugging (proposal in SERV-7890).

Open questions / discussion items:
- Is the small MMLU regression from GPTQ acceptable for PLG-hosted defaults? We need product input on acceptable delta thresholds.
- Prioritization: optimize AWQ kernel path vs roll GPTQ widely — both are viable but resources limited.

Appendix: artifacts we produced during profiling:
- Nsight traces for 7B GPTQ run (link in linked_artifacts)
- nvtx-marked timeline + token-level latencies attached to PR 412
- calibration scripts + representative calibration set in repo under /bench/quant-calib/

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a snapshot of experiments run in Jan 2025 on the quant-bench-2025 branch. Numbers are median-ish from small-run experiments; we should not treat them as final SLA targets.
- Please review kernel/packing recommendations and sign off on which quant presets we push to hosted default.

-- Jordan
